body:
OverviewViewModelTest fails intermittently with
`java.lang.IllegalStateException at TestMainDispatcher.kt:72` (sometimes
`UncompletedCoroutinesError`), on different test methods across different
runs — not a specific test's logic, a class-wide race. Confirmed
nondeterministic: identical code, back-to-back runs, one run failed one
test and passed on immediate re-run with zero changes; caught again by
T-56's verify-all.sh full-suite run (a different test method failed that
time).

Root cause (diagnosed, not yet fixed): `MainDispatcherRule`
(app/src/test/java/org/p23q/shoppinglist/MainDispatcherRule.kt) creates
its own `UnconfinedTestDispatcher()`, NOT tied to the `TestCoroutineScheduler`
that each test's own `runTest { }` block creates internally. Two
independent virtual-time schedulers exist per test — `viewModelScope`
coroutines run on the Rule's dispatcher/scheduler, while `runTest`'s
`advanceUntilIdle`/completion tracking watches its own. Under certain
interleavings the two race, producing the observed exceptions.

Fix: `MainDispatcherRule` should accept and install a dispatcher backed by
the *same* scheduler the enclosing `runTest` uses, not a standalone one —
e.g. thread the `TestScope`'s dispatcher through, or restructure so the
rule and `runTest` share one `TestCoroutineScheduler`. Verify by running
OverviewViewModelTest repeatedly (a loop, not just twice) both in
isolation and inside the full suite, since isolation alone didn't
reproduce it in this session's investigation — needs the full-suite load
or repeated runs to surface reliably.
title: Android: OverviewViewModelTest is flaky (MainDispatcherRule / runTest dispatcher race)
